channel.title: eala energy — Insights
channel.description: Insights from eala energy on distributed AI compute, curtailed renewable power and the energy-resilience layer.

item.title: Why long money doesn’t go where the curtailment is
item.description: Behind the Scottish constraint, a battery may have three to five strong years; lenders want seven to ten. What kind of project fits that window?

item.title: How many hours can Britain’s batteries actually store?
item.description: Britain’s 8.7 GW battery fleet holds 14.1 GWh, about an hour and a half at full output. Why storage duration, and a load at the node, matter.

item.title: Is the battery party over?
item.description: GB battery revenues hit £99k/MW a year in September, yet Norway’s oil fund says values are falling. Location, not chemistry, decided who won.

item.title: Are we using the batteries we already have?
item.description: This summer batteries offered the grid twice as much energy as last year; under 6% was dispatched. The case for giving storage a job of its own.

item.title: Capital isn’t scarce. A place on the wires is.
item.description: €270m for 350 MW at Kilmarnock South, and Ofgem plans a fee to hold a connection queue place. What’s scarce now is grid access, not capital.

item.title: Stop waiting for a socket
item.description: 90 GW of batteries built or queued against 29 GW needed by 2035, and soon a fee to stay in line. Why storage and compute behind a wind farm can build now.
